[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

'''⚠️ Paleographic Warning:'''

This profile is based on a testament written in 16th-century Secretary Hand. Due to the ornate and inconsistent handwriting style, all names, places, and relationships should be considered '''tentative''' and subject to '''revision''' pending further document comparison or corroboration. Interpretations are paleographically informed but speculative.

== Biography ==
'''Archibald Glasgow''' was baptized on 20 March 1618 in South Leith, Edinburghshire, the son of [[Glasgow-3075|William Glasgow (bef.1600–)]] and [[Fraser-15286|Catherine (Fraser) Glasgow (1600–)]].<ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FQM4-LYL : 12 February 2020), Archbald Glascow, 1618.</ref>

=== Parentage ===

Four records identify Archibald as the son of [[Glasgow-3075|William Glasgow]], mealmaker in Leith. His 1618 baptism names William as his father. On 23 October 1639 the Edinburgh apprentice register called Archibald the son of William Glasgow, mealmaker in Leith, when he was apprenticed to Thomas Park, cordiner.<ref>Francis J. Grant, ed., ''Register of Apprentices of the City of Edinburgh, 1583-1666'', Scottish Record Society 28 (1906), [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso28scotuoft/page/71/mode/2up p. 71], 23 October 1639.</ref> William's testament dative, confirmed on 22 July 1646, says that William died in September 1644 and was given up by Archibald Glasgow, his lawful son and sole executor dative.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, CC8/8/62, images 461–462, testament dative and inventory of William Glasgow, mealmaker in Leith, confirmed 22 July 1646; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/search-records/legal-records/wills Scotland's People wills search].</ref> On 1 May 1647 Archibald was served heir to William; the retour abstract again described Archibald as a shoemaker in Leith and William as a mealmaker there, expressly calling William his father.<ref>Great Britain Record Commission, ''Inquisitionum ad Capellam Domini Regis Retornatarum... Abbreviatio'', vol. 2 (1811), Inquisitiones Generales, no. 3278, 1 May 1647, original retour xix.128, [https://archive.org/details/inquisitionumadc00grea_0 Internet Archive].</ref>

He is possibly the same '''Archibald Glasgow''' who appears in multiple mid-17th century records associated with Leith:

* On 14 April 1646, Archibald Glasgow married '''Margaret Hilstones''' in South Leith.<ref>Scotland Marriages 1561–1910, OPR Marriages, South Leith, 692/2, 90/310. Entry: Archbald Glasgow and Margaret Hilstones, 14 April 1646.</ref>

* A child named [[Glasgow-2714|George Glasgow (bef.1658–)]] was born in 1658 in South Leith to parents named '''Archibald Glasgow''' and '''Agnes Watson'''.<ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950", FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FQMH-CXH : 12 February 2020), Georg Glasgowe, 1658.</ref> This may indicate a second marriage or a clerical discrepancy in the mother’s recorded name.

* On 24 May 1662, an '''Archibald Glasgow, maltman and indweller in Leith''' is referenced in a testament recorded in the Edinburgh Commissary Court (CC8/8/70). This legal record, associated with the inventory of his estate, confirms his occupation and residency in Leith during this period.

Given the overlap of dates, location, and naming patterns, it is plausible that all these records refer to the same individual—'''Archibald Glasgow, maltman of Leith'''—though further evidence is needed to confirm each connection definitively.

== Research Notes ==
=== Leith–Kilwinning working family ===

Select Archibald [[Glasgow-3078]] as George [[Glasgow-3120]]’s possible working father at 43% subjective confidence, through possible identity with the Leith child George [[Glasgow-2714]]. The unattached George is the record-defined father with Jannet Willie at Kilwinning in 1688. His own biography cross-references George-2714, and Marie’s biography already links that other George as her father while her structured field names George-3120. These are dependent inherited identity suggestions, not independent historical witnesses. The 1658 child would be about twenty at the recorded 1678 Kilwinning marriage and thirty at Marie’s 1688 baptism. The latter George account’s circa-1660 birth is only an estimate and does not exclude the 1658 child. Prefer this already identified childhood/father route to inventing a new parent or treating the two George accounts as demonstrably unrelated.

The 43% rates the whole proposed father link to the 1688 adult, including the unresolved childhood and household identities. No record names that adult’s parents or carries the Leith child to Kilwinning. Jean Gardiner, Isobell/Jonet Young and Jannet Willie remain separately recorded women; no remarriage, alias or combined household is established. Another local George or another father remains possible. George-1082 of Mid Calder, George-1090 of Glasgow, George-1560 of Linlithgow and George-3100 of Campbeltown remain weaker chronological comparisons; different recorded settings and missing later records are not exclusions. Keep George-3120 and George-2714 as separate accounts and retain all spouses and children; the added son account does not establish two distinct George sons of Archibald. Agnes Watsone is named as the 1658 child’s mother, but no maternal attachment is selected for George-3120 in this paternal working comparison. Existing mothers, all vital fields and the uncertainty of Archibald’s own wider identity are preserved.

The record-defined father of the 1658 child George-2714 is assessed at 98%; the record-defined father George-3120 of Marie-3090 is assessed at 98%. These named record roles do not establish the childhood or migration identity of the 1688 adult. George-2714’s live father is already marked certain; no pending father-certainty upgrade is counted for him. Marie’s attached father is currently unmarked, so her proposed confident mark is separate from George-3120’s new possible father.

The useful next test is a household or occupational identifier in the original 1678 marriage and 1688 baptism, followed by Leith/Kilwinning apprenticeship, property or testament evidence. Check the two 1683 maternal index readings before combining Gardiner and Young. The original 1662 Archibald testament names a lawful son George, but does not identify his later adult residence.<ref name="LeithKilwinning2026">[https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4518492&tab=this Leith George, 16 May 1658; Ard Glasgow and Agnes Watsone, OPR 692/2/2 item 2]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_685338879&tab=this Marie, Kilwinning baptism 29 July 1688; George Glasgow and Jannet Willie]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_694398730%2F1&tab=this Gorg Glasgow and Jean Gardiner, Kilwinning marriage index 8 November 1678]. Transcripts inspected18 October2026, original images uninspected; repeated indexes describe the same underlying events.</ref>
